result.final_text:
## What this letter says

You fell at home and hit your head on 14 October 2026. You were checked in the Emergency Department.

You did not lose consciousness (you did not black out).

The doctors did tests:
- X-ray of your right hip: no fracture (no break)
- CT scan of your head: no bleeding inside your head

They found your blood pressure drops when you stand up. When lying down it was 142/80. When standing it was 108/66.

This drop in blood pressure may have caused your fall.

## What you need to do

1. Stop taking amlodipine 10 mg daily. It may be making your blood pressure drop.
2. Continue taking all your other medicines.
3. Stand up slowly from sitting or lying down.
4. Sit on the edge of the bed for 1 minute before standing.
5. You have been referred to the Falls Prevention Clinic. They will write to you with an appointment.
6. Your doctor should check your blood pressure again in 4 weeks.

## Dates and medicines

**Medicine change**:
- STOP: amlodipine 10 mg daily - it may be making your blood pressure drop when you stand.
- Continue all your other medicines as before.

**Appointment date**:
- You were seen at the Emergency Department on 14 October 2026.

## Questions to ask your doctor

1. Why does my blood pressure drop when I stand up?
2. When should I check about stopping amlodipine?
3. What medicines can I take instead of amlodipine?
4. How will we know if the amlodipine was the problem?

## When to get urgent help

If you develop a worsening headache, vomiting, confusion or drowsiness in the next few days, call 999 or go to A&E.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
